title: introduce-tenant-geo-locker-consent-driven-kms-routing-and-audit-signer
author: Priya Menon
body:
Motivation: customers operating across regulated jurisdictions require deterministic tenant-level key routing and an auditable consent surface. This PR introduces a tenant "geo-locker" that pins KMS usage to region-asserted key anchors, a consent-forwarding bridge for operator workflows, and a tamper-evident audit signer to make audit records non-repudiable.

What this PR does (high level):
- Adds a tenant-scoped KMS routing layer that resolves preferred key endpoints based on tenant residency claims and policy overrides.
- Implements a consent bridge: when an operator or automated workflow needs cross-region key use, the bridge records consent assertions and attaches consent handles to requests.
- Adds an audit signer component that signs audit envelopes (ED25519) and includes signature metadata in the audit pipeline for downstream immutable storage.
- Wires new policy checks into RBAC v2 decision flow so cross-region key use is flagged and can be gated by consent.

Design notes:
- The geo-locker resolver is intentionally policy-driven: tenant residency metadata (provided at provisioning) + per-tenant allowlists produce an ordered preference list for KMS endpoints. The resolver is pluggable for future multi-provider mapping.
- Consent bridge maintains short-lived consent handles (opaque tokens) and an operator audit entry. Consent tokens are single-use and TTL-bound.
- Audit signer produces a compact signature header and a signature manifest that can be attached or stored alongside existing audit logs. The manifest includes key id, signer version, and canonicalized payload hash.

Compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior preserves current KMS routing; geo-locker is opt-in per-tenant.
- Feature flag: features.geo_locker.enabled = false by default. We will enable in a staggered rollout: internal dogfood tenants -> opt-in customers -> enforced for regulated tenants.
- Backwards-compatible: when consent handles are absent, cross-region requests follow current fallback rules but are logged with reason=unconsented.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for resolver policy logic, consent token lifecycle, and signer output canonicalization.
- Integration test harness simulating cross-region request paths with a fake KMS endpoint and a signed-audit store.
- Load-tested signer at 10k/sec signing throughput in perf-canary cluster; signer adds ~2ms median latency when batched.

Security considerations:
- Signer keys are stored in HSM-backed KMS; the signer fetches a short-lived signing key via internal KMS assume role flow.
- Consent tokens are opaque and cannot be forged; they include a MAC tied to the tenant and operator id.
- RBAC v2 checks are extended; misconfiguration will log with metric rbac.geo_lock_denied to alert on accidental denies.

Checklist:
- [x] Add resolver and policy evaluation layer
- [x] Add consent bridge and token lifecycle
- [x] Add audit signer component and manifest format
- [x] Integrate RBAC v2 checks and metrics
- [x] Add unit + integration tests
- [x] Add feature flag and rollout plan

Related: Linear ENG-3127, ENG-3184. Jira: SUP-1429 (support case that drove TTL behavior).

review_comments: Darren Liu: Can we avoid a hot-path call to KMS for signer key retrieval on every request? Suggest caching short-lived keys and adding retries with jitter.
Priya Menon: Answered - signer caches a 5m ephemeral key retrieved via internal KMS assume role flow; added tests and a backoff wrapper (see signer.go).
Sofia Martinez: RBAC change looks good, but we need clearer metric tags for multi-tenant alerting (added rbac.geo_lock_denied.{tenant,region}).
Ethan Park: Please add a doc note about operational recovery when consent-store DB is unavailable.
release_notes: Add tenant geo-locker: opt-in tenant-level KMS routing, consent bridge for cross-region key use, and tamper-evident audit signer. Feature behind flag; see admin guide for rollout steps.
notes_for_oncall: If audit signer begins failing, fallback mode will mark audit records as unsigned and emit metric audit_signer.failures. Oncall should check signer/key access, KMS assume-role logs, and consent-store health. Temporary mitigation: toggle features.geo_locker.enabled=false to skip routing and signer enforcement.
